question.question:
Apply only this fictional scenario-local key-rotation policy. Day 1 starts with a fresh key active. The key rotates at the end of every 5-th day (end of day 5, 2x5, ...); records on a rotation day use the outgoing key, and the new key covers the next day onward. The active key is compromised on day 21, exposing every record encrypted with it from the day after its last rotation through day 21 inclusive. Day 1 has 13900 records; each later day has -200 more than the prior day (negative means fewer). Cost per exposed record is 0.5 US cents. A regulatory adjustment of 200 basis points of the base exposure cost is then added (negative reduces it). Report exposure window days, exposed records, base cost in USD, and total exposure cost in USD.

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 2 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `usd` with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Number of days in the exposure window including the compromise day
Total records encrypted during the exposure window
Exposure cost in USD before the basis-point adjustment
